name: bid_ask_imbalance_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: When the bid-side depth significantly exceeds ask-side depth (or vice versa) at the top 5 levels of the order book, the resulting imbalance predicts short-term price movement in the direction of the heavier side. This inefficiency exists because most retail participants trade market orders and ignore the order book, while institutional algorithms that exploit this signal operate on sub-millisecond timescales not accessible to 1-min bar traders. At the 1-min timescale, the signal persists because aggregated imbalance over 1-min windows captures sustained directional pressure from large participants building positions, not just fleeting spoofing. The edge survives because it requires real-time L2 data processing, which most Indian retail traders lack, and the signal decays within 3-5 bars, making it unattractive to slower systematic funds.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, bid-ask spread < 5 bps, tick size ≤ 0.05
session: 09:20-15:15 IST (skip first 5 min and last 15 min)

other: L2 order book snapshot every 1 sec aggregated to 1-min

indicators.name: bid_ask_imbalance
indicators.formula: BAI = (sum(bid_qty, levels=5) - sum(ask_qty, levels=5)) / (sum(bid_qty, levels=5) + sum(ask_qty, levels=5))

entry.entry_price: limit order at best bid (long) or best ask (short)

exit.time_stop: exit if no target hit within 5 bars

risk.position_sizing: fixed notional ₹1L per trade, reduce to ₹50K when VIX > 18

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; reduce size by 50% when VIX in 18-22
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 5 min (09:15-09:20) or last 15 min (15:15-15:30)
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy days, budget day, F&O expiry day
other_filters: skip if stock is in upper/lower circuit limit

edge.edge_decay_risk: High — as more brokers offer L2 data APIs and algo adoption grows in India, this signal will get crowded. Expected half-life of edge: 12-18 months.

weaknesses: L2 order book data in India is noisy and prone to spoofing/layering, especially in mid-cap names. The signal may be corrupted by phantom orders.
Zerodha does not provide raw L2 depth via Kite API beyond 5 levels; signal quality degrades without deeper book visibility.
High-frequency market makers will front-run this signal at sub-second timescales, leaving only residual edge for 1-min bar traders.
prior_art: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014) 'The Price Impact of Order Book Events' establishes the theoretical foundation. Cartea, Jaimungal & Penalva (2015) extend to optimal execution. In the Indian context, limited academic work exists but NSE's co-location framework suggests institutional participants already exploit this.
notes: Requires real-time L2 data subscription. Backtesting is difficult because historical order book snapshots are not widely available for Indian equities. Paper trade for at least 30 days before live deployment. Consider using NSE's TBT (tick-by-tick) data feed if available.
